direction: A physics-based cost function for trajectory optimisation: penalise mechanical energy injected into the system (or deviation from a target energy level) instead of, or in addition to, the usual quadratic state and control cost. Test on pendulum and cart-pole swing-up with iLQR or shooting-based MPC written in numpy. Compare against the standard quadratic cost and against the classic energy-shaping controller: success rate over random initial states, control effort, time to upright, and sensitivity to cost weights.

notes.note: fix round: H2 caveat with paired sweep table and tuned comparison, term diagnostic, font/figures/tables, method details

decisions.decision: Searched control/energy swing-up literature; no controlled head-to-head found; claims kept modest. Chose Gauss-Newton iLQR with clipped controls, point-mass pole, cart force limit 8 (15 made the task trivial in a pilot on tuning seed 100).
